articles.title: Polaroid’s new instant camera has four creative shooting modes you can experiment with
articles.summary: Polaroid’s Mod is a new instant camera with four different shooting modes creating analog effects like double exposures and light trails.
articles.body: Polaroid announced a new instant camera that lets photographers get more creative and experimental with their shots than just changing the aperture or shutter speed. In addition to a Brightness dial on the front for adjusting exposure, the new Polaroid Mod has a dial around the lens for switching between four “creative shooting modes” with unique analog effects that are all captured in-camera. The Polaroid Mod is launching globally starting today for $169.99 through Polaroid’s online store and will be available from other US retailers on October 6th. Two of the modes combine multiple exposures into one image using a simple process that involves capturing two separate exposures, one after the other, when prompted by the camera. Double Exposure layers two images atop each other to blend subjects or scenes together while Split Shot divides images into two halves using a rotating accessory that blocks half the lens at a time. [Image: Motion Freeze mode (left) merges a slow shutter exposure with a sharp one captured by the camera’s flash while Double Exposure mode (right) layers two exposures atop each other. Light Painting uses a long exposure to capture light trails from a flashlight, sparkler, or other bright source while the camera is perched atop a stable tripod to keep other static elements in frame from becoming blurred. Motion Freeze is Polaroid’s name for the second curtain sync or rear curtain flash feature found in other cameras. A slower shutter speed is used to capture motion trails of a moving subject that’s combined with a sharp image of them captured by firing the Mod’s flash at the end of the exposure. [Image: On the front of the Mod, you’ll find a dial for adjusting exposure and a second around the lens for switching between the four creative modes. The Polaroid Mod works with Polaroid i-Type and 600 film stocks in color or black and white, and on a full charge of its 750mAh battery it can shoot up to 15 packs of film, which is up to 120 exposures. It uses a fixed focus two-lens system with a 103mm standard lens and a 95mm portrait lens that can be swapped as needed depending on the subject.

articles.title: Oura shelves its $2.2B IPO, citing 'uncertainty' in the market | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The postponement of the IPO will delay some of the company's plans for its proceeds from the IPO, as well as those of its shareholders.
articles.body:
Smart ring maker Oura has postponed its up to $2.2 billion IPO indefinitely, citing “uncertainty in the IPO market.”

The company, which had filed to offer 55 million shares at a range of $40 to $44 each in the IPO, did not provide additional details. The IPO would have valued Oura at up to $15 billion at the midpoint of that range.

“Our mission is to empower people to live healthier, longer, and an IPO is just one step in our journey. We aim to deliver an extraordinary IPO for our employees and investors and we have the luxury of choosing our moment. In the meantime, we will execute against the opportunities ahead,” the company’s CEO, Tom Hale, said in a statement .

Indeed, Oura seems to be doing well. The company said that its latest product, the Oura Ring 5, has been received well in the market, and it now has 5.7 million paying members, up from 5 million at the end of June. The company expects overall revenue to increase 90% in its 2026 financial year compared to a year earlier, when it had revenue of $907.9 million.

The postponement of the IPO, however, will delay some of the company’s plans for proceeds that would have been generated from the IPO, as well as those of its shareholders.

Forerunner Ventures, an early investor in Oura, was slated to sell all of its 9.3% stake in the IPO, which would have net it about $1.20 billion (assuming the shares listed at the $42 midpoint). Oura, meanwhile, intended to use most of the IPO proceeds to pay off tax obligations related to employee share grants that would have vested at the listing.

Any shareholders looking for liquidity will also have to wait now.

Oura’s valuation has risen fast in recent years. Oura was valued at about $11 billion last October when it raised $900 million in a round led by Fidelity, roughly double the $5.2 billion valuation it carried less than a year earlier. Its business has also leaned increasingly into recurring revenue. Memberships carry an 89% gross margin and made up about 20% of sales in the latest period, though hardware still generates most of the revenue. Oura had about $372 million in cash at the end of June, which it planned to leave untouched by using IPO proceeds to cover employee-related tax obligations.

articles.title: Apple's $250M Siri settlement: How to claim up to $95
articles.summary: The $250 million Apple Siri AI settlement is now accepting claims, with eligible iPhone owners potentially receiving up to $95 per device.
articles.body: If you bought one of Apple's AI-ready iPhones because you expected the smarter Siri Apple had been talking about, check when you purchased it. You could have some money coming your way. A proposed $250 million Apple Siri settlement now has an open claims process for qualifying iPhone owners. The case centers on allegations that consumers bought certain iPhones expecting Siri features powered by Apple Intelligence that they did not receive during the period covered by the lawsuit. Apple denies the allegations and says it did nothing improper or unlawful. The amount may sound small next to the price of a new iPhone, but filing a claim could put as much as $95 per eligible device back in your pocket. There are a few important catches, though, including exactly which iPhone you bought and when you bought it. Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed. Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com 8 BIGGEST THINGS WE LEARNED FROM APPLE'S 2026 EVENT Why Apple agreed to a $250 million Siri settlement The lawsuit is called Landsheft, et al. v. Apple Inc. and is pending in federal court in Northern California. The plaintiffs alleged that Apple promoted certain Siri features powered by Apple Intelligence, leading buyers to expect capabilities that were not delivered during the class period. Apple denies those allegations. The company agreed to put $250 million into a settlement fund rather than continue litigating the case. The agreement received preliminary court approval on July 17, 2026. The court has scheduled a final approval hearing for Feb. 24, 2027. That timing is especially interesting because Apple finally began rolling out its long-awaited Siri AI beta with iOS 27 in September 2026. The updated Siri can use personal context from information on your device, handle follow-up questions and take more actions inside supported apps. We recently took a closer look at iOS 27 and the new Siri AI features. Which iPhones qualify for the Apple Siri settlement? The settlement covers seven models: iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, iPhone 16, iPhone 16e, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro and iPhone 16 Pro Max. The regular iPhone 15 and iPhone 15 Plus are excluded. Owning one of those eligible models alone does not qualify you. You must be the original purchaser and live in the United States. You also must have purchased the phone in the United States between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025. The purchase had to be for personal or business use rather than resale. There is another important requirement. When you submit the claim, you must confirm that you expected to receive certain Siri Apple Intelligence features when you bought the device and did not receive those features as expected. Businesses can qualify, too. The official settlement site has separate filing options for individuals and organizations that purchased eligible devices for business use. How much could you receive from the Apple settlement? The settlement sets the payment at $25 per eligible device, but the final amount can change. If fewer valid claims come in, the payment may increase to as much as $95 per eligible device. If more claims come in, the payment can fall below $25. Administrative costs, approved attorneys' fees and other court-approved expenses also come out of the $250 million fund. You can submit a claim for each eligible device you purchased. That could make the payout more meaningful for someone who bought multiple qualifying iPhones during the class period. However, nobody knows the final payment yet. The settlement administrator has to count and validate the claims before that figure can be determined. 12 BIGGEST APPLE WWDC 2026 TAKEAWAYS YOU NEED TO KNOW How to file your Apple Siri settlement claim The claims period officially opened on Sept. 21, 2026. You can file through the official Smartphone AI Settlement website at smartphoneaisettlement.com. The deadline is Dec. 21, 2026. The claim form asks for your contact information and information that can confirm your eligible purchase or ownership. You also need to certify that you expected the covered Siri Apple Intelligence features when you purchased your iPhone and did not receive them as expected. I would have your iPhone's serial number handy before you start. On your iPhone, open Settings, tap General, then tap About. Your serial number appears near the top of that screen. You can press and hold it to copy it. The settlement site also says you may find the serial number on the phone's original packaging or purchase documentation. Do you need to have received a settlement notice? The official site says people who received an email or postcard can file a claim. It also says people who believe they belong to the settlement class can submit a valid claim even if they did not receive a notice. So, I would not automatically write this off because nothing showed up in your mailbox or inbox. Instead, compare your purchase with the eligibility requirements and use the official settlement site. Be careful with links arriving through unexpected texts or emails. Large settlements often attract phishing attempts because scammers know people are looking for claim information. I recommend going directly to the official settlement website rather than clicking a claim link in an unsolicited message. When will iPhone owners actually get paid? Do not expect a payment right after submitting your claim. The court has scheduled its final approval hearing for Feb. 24, 2027. The judge will decide whether to give the settlement final approval. Appeals could delay the process further. The official settlement administrator says payments will be processed after the settlement becomes effective, assuming the court approves it and any appeals are resolved. In other words, filing now secures your claim before the deadline. The check or digital payment could come much later. YOU COULD GET PAID FROM GOOGLE’S ANDROID DATA LAWSUIT What if you do nothing? If you qualify but do nothing, you will not receive a settlement payment. You will also remain bound by the settlement if the court gives it final approval, which affects your ability to pursue your own case against Apple over the claims covered by this lawsuit. The deadline to request exclusion from the settlement or formally object is also Dec. 21, 2026. Anyone considering those options should read the official settlement notice carefully because the legal consequences differ from simply submitting a claim. CyberGuy reached out to Apple for additional comment but did not hear back before our deadline. Kurt's key takeaways Apple spent a lot of time building excitement around what Apple Intelligence would bring to Siri. If you bought one of these iPhones expecting those promised features, you may have been left waiting much longer than expected. Apple has now agreed to put $250 million into a settlement fund while continuing to deny the allegations. If your iPhone and purchase date qualify, I would take a few minutes to check your eligibility and file a claim. You could receive as much as $95 per device, depending on how many valid claims come in. This is also a good reminder to pay close attention when a company promotes upcoming software features as part of the reason to buy new hardware. What you are promised at launch and what you can actually use on day one may be very different. articles.body: John Ternus, Apple’s new CEO, wants Apple to launch products more often than its usual splashy moments in the fall and the spring, according to a Bloomberg report detailing some of Ternus’s initial plans for the company. Apple regularly holds iPhone launch events in September and often announces products later in the year and in springtime, but “Ternus has indicated that Apple must introduce products more quickly and become more experimental to remain competitive in the artificial intelligence era,” Bloomberg says. The shift may not happen right away given Apple’s “long-established” development practices. Apple is rumored to have a considerable number of products in the pipeline, including a new HomePod Mini, iPad Mini, and Apple TV 4K, AirPods with cameras, touchscreen MacBooks, and a special 20th anniversary iPhone. Ternus is also considering reducing layers between engineers and senior executives, and the hardware engineering team dismissed “a number” of engineering program managers in the past two weeks, Bloomberg says. Apple also apparently considered laying off 5,000 AppleCare customer service staffers, but “ultimately put those plans on hold.”
